questions.question: What are factories (FactoryBot) in Rails testing?
questions.title: Factories (FactoryBot) Intro
questions.direct_answer: Factories build test objects with valid default data so tests are terse and realistic. `FactoryBot.define do; factory :user do; name { 'Al' }; email { 'a@x.com' }; role { 'user' }; end; end` then `create(:user)` makes a saved User with defaults; `build(:user)` makes an unsaved one; `create(:user, role: 'admin')` overrides. Versus fixtures (static YAML data in test DB): factories are more flexible (override per-test, associations, traits) and don't require shared global state, but fixtures are faster for stable data. Use factories for unit/integration tests where you need fresh, specific records. Traits (`factory :user; trait :admin do; role { 'admin' }; end`) compose variations (`create(:user, :admin)`). Associations: `factory :post do; user; end` builds a linked user. Keep factories lean (only required fields + a few realistic ones) so tests stay fast and clear; avoid over-generating data you don't use.

sections.title: Factories
sections.content:
build test objects with valid defaults. create (saved), build (unsaved), traits. vs fixtures (faster but shared). Lean factories.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  D[factory :user] --> C[create(:user) saved]
  B[build(:user)] --> U[unsaved]
  T[trait :admin] --> V[create(:user, :admin)]
  A[association: user] --> L[builds linked user]
```

sections.title: Factories (FactoryBot)
sections.content:
```ruby
# spec/factories.rb (or spec/factories/*.rb)
FactoryBot.define do
  factory :user do
    name  { 'Al' }                 # default valid values
    email { 'a@x.com' }
    role  { 'user' }
  end

  factory :post do
    title  { 'Hello' }
    user                  # association: builds (and on create, saves) a linked user
  end
end

# In tests:
user = create(:user)                  # saved User with defaults
user = build(:user)                   # unsaved (in-memory) User
user = create(:user, role: 'admin')   # override a field
post = create(:post, user: user)      # override association

# Traits: composable variations
factory :user do
  role { 'user' }
  trait :admin do; role { 'admin' }; end
  trait :banned do; banned { true }; end
end
create(:user, :admin)                 # role: 'admin'
create(:user, :admin, :banned)        # both traits

# Factories vs fixtures:
#   fixtures  -> static YAML, pre-loaded into the test DB; FAST but SHARED across tests
#   factories -> build per-test; flexible (override, traits, associations) but slower
# Use factories for fresh, specific records; fixtures for stable shared data.

# Keep factories LEAN: only required fields + a few realistic ones.
#   avoid over-generating (slower tests, brittle). Override per test as needed.
FactoryBot.modify do  # tweak an existing factory
  factory :user do; age { 30 }; end
end
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Over-stuffing factories with data the test doesn't need (slow, brittle) — keep them lean.
Sharing fixtures across tests (hidden coupling; a change breaks many tests).
Hardcoding values that should vary (use sequences for unique emails).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Factories (FactoryBot) build test objects with valid default data.
create(:user) saves with defaults; build(:user) is unsaved; override with create(:user, role: 'admin').
Traits compose variations: create(:user, :admin); associations build linked records.
Versus fixtures: factories are flexible (per-test) but slower; fixtures are fast but shared.
Keep factories lean (only required + a few realistic fields) so tests stay fast and clear.
